newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Colonial to reduce capital by cancelling shrs.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Colonial to reduce capital by cancelling shrs.

text.p: The Colonial Motor Company said on Wednesday it would reduce capital in the company by returning capital to shareholders.
Colonial's directors proposed at the Annual General Meeting to cancel four out of every five Colonial shares, paying shareholders NZ$0.50 for each share cancelled.
The directors said the move was consistent with the drive to maximise value to shareholders.

"In order to avoid a significant increase in the company's share price resulting from the lesser number of shares on issue, the directors propose that the remaining shares be subdivided into shares with a par value of 10 cents, immediately upon the capital reduction taking effect," the directors said in a statement.

"This will ensure that the number of shares on issue before and after the capital reduction remains the same so that shareholders are able to make a meaningful comparison of the financial performance of the company from year to year."

The capital reduction must be approved by a special resolution of shareholders and be confirmed by the High Court. An Extraordinary General Meeting will be held in the first quarter of 1997 to consider the proposed return of capital.
If shareholders approve the move, the company expects to make the payment in April.
